Main Storyline：
Players will take on the role of a warrior of the Red Church, led by the great leader Maxwell, to defeat powerful reactionary enemies.

Game Size：
The game includes a total of 6 main levels. Except for the main city level of Lonserf, each level is massive and features traditional Souls-like sandbox levels. The game includes a total of 10 boss battles and over 80 different AI combat encounters.

Voiceover & Subtitles：
The game includes both Chinese and English voiceovers, with multi-language subtitles.

Key Features：

  • Diverse enemy attack moves
    Basic combo attacks, dangerous strikes, fatal attacks

  • Multi-layered enemy counter mechanisms and rewards
    Mikiri counter, dodge, parry, gun counter, riposte

  • An epic and stirring historical adventure storyline
    Multiple church factions compete for the right to lead Gurettvo, involving conspiracies, grudges, grand historical trends, and the victory of ideals and beliefs.

  • Various items, skills, and martial arts to "abuse" bosses

detailed_description:
#label_roadmapTest Release: Our First Announcement

Dear players, we are Parry Frames. As this is our first time launching a game on Steam, we want to test sending our first announcement. One purpose is to test the announcement function, another is to introduce ourselves, and finally, to address some community feedback.

Introduction to Red Soul

First, allow us to briefly introduce our team's game Red Soul—a Souls-like title that blends mechanics from multiple Souls games. Most of the development team are passionate fans of Souls games, and the producer's initial inspiration to create a game actually stemmed from Dark Souls 3. This not only determined that we would make a Souls-like game but also influenced our choice: for a micro-team like ours, it requires lower technical complexity, and additionally, it reduces communication costs—everyone easily aligns on design directions. The original goal of creating a decent Souls-like game has been the internal driving force for the team to tackle technical challenges one by one.

Clarification on Game Mechanics

While many of our game mechanics draw inspiration from Souls games, we emphasize that this is not direct copying or replication. Based on our understanding of the original combat systems, we’ve innovated new battle mechanics. During promotion, we use phrases like "similar to X" to help players quickly grasp the mechanics, but make no mistake—Red Soul introduces micro-innovations rather than being a 复刻 (replication). Some mechanics and gameplay require players to build new understanding, as direct application of Souls game experience may not work.

  • Parry Mechanic: Similar to Sekiro’s blade deflection but with key differences. In Sekiro, holding block maintains a continuous state for blocking or parrying, while Red Soul triggers a fixed parry animation upon pressing the button. Thus, "Ashina Cross" tactics won’t work here—players must observe the enemy’s attack rhythm and time their parry just before impact, the classic "one hit, one parry" approach.

  • Dangerous Attacks: Like Sekiro’s "危" moves but with distinct variations. Our dangerous attacks can be identified by their direction, countered via a "gun parry" mechanic or specific special moves.

  • Desperate Attacks: Inspired by Nioh’s finishing moves, these are powerful strikes or throws that ignore all defenses. Players must dodge or retreat to avoid them.

Eight Years in the Making

The producer, a self-taught game developer with no formal education or prior experience, was inspired to create a Souls-like game after playing Dark Souls 3—a dream that’s lasted nearly 8 years. In March 2018, they began learning game engines, researching UE, Unity, Godot, etc., and chose Unreal Engine for its accessible visuals and marketplace assets.

The project officially started 4 years ago. Notably, the team has adhered to 95% of the original 50,000-word design document, including detailed roadmaps for mechanics. While the final script is only ~20,000 words, discarded drafts total over 100,000 words. This thorough upfront planning—defining features and details—has been crucial to bringing the game to fruition.

Message from the Producer

  • Release Date: Red Soul will launch on October 21, 2025. We’ll finish all levels, combat, story, and quests by late July, then spend 3 months on PlayTest and refinements to ensure quality and fix bugs.

  • Funding Update: Our budget lasts until December 2025. We’ve secured a small 外包 (outsourcing) project with former colleagues and applied for an Epic Grants micro-fund. Even if the grant is denied, the 外包 should sustain us until April 2026. This means:

    • If we need to delay, we’ll prioritize quality over rushing a 半成品.

    • Even if the game underperforms, we’ll refine it until April 2026 before disbanding.

About the Demo (Released June 17)

The current Demo isn’t perfect, but we released it early to address a key issue: internal testers, too familiar with the combat, designed enemies that were overly difficult. Following advice from a hardcore Souls player, we launched the Demo to gather feedback. Already, we’ve received domestic and overseas suggestions, and we’ll update the Demo within a month. Rest assured, the Demo has no game-breaking bugs—feel free to try it!

Stay Tuned for Updates!
— The Parry Frames Team
